answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Like a river that only flows through one verified channel, each identity must post a bond tied to a single auditable history of past work; an ember of reputation earned slowly cannot be faked overnight. If peers detect duplicate or fraudulent behavior, the stake is slashed and the history is burned, so an attacker must pay the full bond for every fake identity instead of echoing one cheap credential across thousands of accounts.
